title_en: Matthew Farwell convicted of killing Sandra Birchmore, unborn child
title_zh: 马修·法威尔因杀害未出生的孩子桑德拉·伯奇莫尔而被定罪
summary: A jury has found former Stoughton, Massachusetts, police officer Matthew Farwell guilty of killing Sandra Birchmore and her unborn child.
summary_zh: 陪审团裁定马萨诸塞州斯托顿市前警官马修·法韦尔杀害桑德拉·伯奇莫尔和她未出生的孩子有罪。
body_en: Matthew Farwell convicted of killing Sandra Birchmore and unborn child in Massachusetts murder trial - CBS News

A jury has found former Stoughton, Massachusetts, police officer Matthew Farwell guilty of killing Sandra Birchmore and her unborn child. The verdict was read in federal court in South Boston Tuesday afternoon.
Farwell was charged with killing a witness or victim and causing the death of an unborn child. He pleaded not guilty. The jury had previously said in a note on Monday that it was "in a deadlock."
There were gasps from Birchmore's family as the verdict was read aloud in court.

Farwell faces a mandatory sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole. Sentencing is scheduled for Feb. 3, 2027. The Department of Justice could have pursued the death penalty against Farwell, but decided last year it would not.

Jurors heard from 50 witnesses over four weeks of testimony. To convict Farwell on the charge of killing a witness or victim, jurors had to find find that he not only killed Birchmore, but that he did so to prevent her from reporting his crimes to federal authorities.

"Today, justice was served for Ms. Sandra Birchmore and her unborn son, both of whom died at the hands of Matthew Farwell. The evidence presented at trial was both shocking and clear," U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Leah Foley said during a news conference, calling Farwell's actions "absolutely diabolical behavior."

Farwell and Birchmore met when she was a 13-year-old cadet in the Stoughton Police Department's youth explorers program. Prosecutors say Farwell began a sexual relationship with her when she was just 15.

The 23-year-old Birchmore was found dead in her Canton apartment with a strap hanging around her neck in February 2021. Her death was initially ruled a suicide. But more than three years later, Farwell was arrested and the medical examiner changed Birchmore's manner of death to "undetermined."

Prosecutors made the case that Farwell strangled Birchmore, who was pregnant with what she believed was his child, and then staged her death to look like a suicide in order to cover up their years-long affair. The defense said Birchmore had a history of mental health problems and committed suicide because Farwell told her he was not the father and the relationship was over.
Barbara Wright, Birchmore's cousin, said she was feeling a mixture of sadness, happiness and relief.

"It's been almost six years since we lost Sandra and let's not forget her baby boy," she said outside court. "We finally got justice. We've been fighting long and hard for her. And she deserves it. She's waited a long time."
Norfolk District Attorney Michael Morrissey said in a statement that he hopes the verdict brings closure to Birchmore's family and friends.
Morrissey's office has faced criticism from Birchmore's loved ones for choosing not to prosecute Farwell on state charges.

"The Norfolk District Attorney's Office (NDAO) recognizes the criticism it has received for its handling of this case. However, its ability to prosecute was constrained by the finding of the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner (OCME) that the manner of death was suicide," the DA said. "The NDAO referred the case to the Attorney General's Office for further review, and at all times worked collaboratively with the federal prosecution, including funding the development of additional evidence. Beginning as early as October of 2022, in an effort to be transparent, the NDAO made public its case file and investigative materials in its possession. We respect the jury's verdict and will have no further comments."
James O'Connor, acting police chief of the Stoughton Police Department, released a statement following the verdict.

"I am grateful for this verdict. It is the outcome Sandra, her unborn child, and her family have deserved for more than five years. The jury heard the evidence and reached a decision, and I fully support it," O'Connor said. "What happened to Sandra is a profound betrayal of the trust every police officer is sworn to uphold. Matthew Farwell used his position to harm someone the community had put in the care of this department. He no longer wears this badge, and he does not represent the men and women of the Stoughton Police Department, who serve this town with honor every day."

Chief Donna McNamara is currently on paid leave from the Stoughton Police Department as part of an investigation not related to the Farwell case. McNamara said in a statement that the verdict is not about Farwell, but instead honoring Birchmore.

"That's what today is about. Today is not just about a verdict. Today is about Sandra. Today a federal jury has confirmed what became apparent to me some time ago, that Sandra was murdered and that her murderer was a police officer who took advantage of her trust and faith in the badge and uniform," McNamara said. "There are those who wanted to forget Sandra Birchmore. But enough people would not remain silent. Enough people spoke up. Enough people asked questions. And rest assured that there are still more questions unanswered than are answered, even after today."
This is a breaking news story that will be updated as more information is available.
body_zh: 马修·法威尔在马萨诸塞州谋杀案审判中杀害桑德拉·伯奇莫尔和未出生的孩子被判有罪 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
陪审团裁定马萨诸塞州斯托顿市前警官马修·法韦尔杀害桑德拉·伯奇莫尔和她未出生的孩子有罪。周二下午，南波士顿联邦法院宣读了该判决。
法韦尔被指控杀害证人或受害者并导致未出生婴儿死亡。他不认罪。陪审团此前在周一的一份报告中表示，目前“陷入僵局”。
当法庭上大声宣读判决时，伯奇莫尔的家人倒吸一口冷气。
法韦尔面临终身监禁的强制性判决，且不得假释。量刑定于 2027 年 2 月 3 日进行。司法部本来可以对法韦尔判处死刑，但去年决定不这样做。
陪审员在四个星期内听取了 50 名证人的证词。为了以杀害证人或受害者的罪名对法韦尔定罪，陪审员必须查明他不仅杀死了伯奇莫尔，而且这样做是为了阻止她向联邦当局举报他的罪行。
马萨诸塞州联邦检察官利亚·福利在新闻发布会上表示，“今天，桑德拉·伯奇莫尔女士和她未出生的儿子都死于马修·法韦尔之手，正义得到了伸张。审判中提供的证据既令人震惊又明确，”她称法韦尔的行为“绝对是恶魔般的行为”。
法韦尔和伯奇莫尔相识时，她 13 岁，还是斯托顿警察局青年探险家项目的一名学员。检察官称，法韦尔在她 15 岁时就开始与她发生性关系。
2021 年 2 月，23 岁的伯奇莫尔被发现死在她位于广州的公寓里，脖子上挂着一条带子。她的死亡最初被裁定为自杀。但三年多后，法韦尔被捕，法医将伯奇莫尔的死亡方式改为“未定”。
检察官称，法韦尔勒死了伯奇莫尔，她认为伯奇莫尔怀着他的孩子，然后将她的死亡装扮成自杀，以掩盖他们多年的恋情。辩方称，伯奇莫尔有精神健康问题史，并自杀了，因为法韦尔告诉她他不是孩子的父亲，两人的关系已经结束。
伯奇莫尔的表弟芭芭拉·赖特 (Barbara Wright) 表示，她的心情既悲伤又幸福，又如释重负。
“我们失去桑德拉已经快六年了，我们不要忘记她的宝贝儿子，”她在法庭外说道。 “我们终于得到了正义。我们为她进行了长期艰苦的斗争。这是她应得的。她已经等了很长时间了。”
诺福克地区检察官迈克尔·莫里西在一份声明中表示，他希望这一判决能够为伯奇莫尔的家人和朋友画上句号。
莫里西的办公室因选择不以国家罪名起诉法韦尔而受到伯奇莫尔亲人的批评。

“诺福克地方检察官办公室（NDAO）承认其在处理此案时受到的批评。然而，其起诉能力受到首席法医办公室（OCME）死亡方式为自杀的调查结果的限制，”地方检察官说。 “NDAO 将此案移交给总检察长办公室进行进一步审查，并始终与联邦检方合作，包括资助更多证据的开发。早在 2022 年 10 月开始，为了保持透明，NDAO 公开了其案件档案和其掌握的调查材料。我们尊重陪审团的裁决，不会发表进一步评论。”
斯托顿警察局代理警察局长詹姆斯·奥康纳在判决后发表了一份声明。
“我很感激这个判决。这是桑德拉、她未出生的孩子和她的家人五年多来应得的结果。陪审团听取了证据并做出了决定，我完全支持它，”奥康纳说。 “发生在桑德拉身上的事情是对每个警察发誓维护的信任的深刻背叛。马修·法韦尔利用他的职位伤害了社区交给这个部门照顾的人。他不再佩戴这个徽章，他不代表斯托顿警察局的男男女女，他们每天都在荣誉地为这个小镇服务。”
斯托顿警察局局长唐娜·麦克纳马拉目前正在带薪休假，以参与与法韦尔案无关的调查。麦克纳马拉在一份声明中表示，这一判决与法韦尔无关，而是为了纪念伯奇莫尔。
“这就是今天的主题。今天不仅仅是一个判决。今天是关于桑德拉的。今天，联邦陪审团证实了我不久前显而易见的事情，即桑德拉被谋杀了，而凶手是一名警察，他利用了她对警徽和制服的信任和信心，”麦克纳马拉说。 “有些人想忘记桑德拉·伯奇莫尔。但有足够多的人不会保持沉默。有足够多的人发声。有足够多的人提出问题。请放心，即使在今天之后，仍然有更多的问题没有得到解答。”
这是一个突发新闻报道，将随着更多信息的出现而更新。

summary: This is part of The Vaccine Divide, an updated data investigation into America potentially losing its measles-free status as the deadly virus roars back and childhood vaccine defenses continue to crack and crumble.

body_en: Measles herd immunity dropping: Check childhood vaccination rates where you live
Measles cases surge to dangerous high as cases top 5,000
By Jiachuan Wu , Jane Weaver , Mustafa Fattah, M.D. , Joe Murphy and Olivia Eckstine

This is part of The Vaccine Divide , an updated data investigation into America potentially losing its measles-free status as the deadly virus roars back and childhood vaccine defenses continue to crack and crumble.
As vaccination rates among children go down, the risk of getting sick from a vaccine-preventable illness such as measles goes up.
Use these maps to see the childhood vaccination rates for your community.

The measles-mumps-rubella vaccine is highly effective in preventing illness in children and adults. To control the spread of measles in a community, a vaccination rate of 95% or higher is needed. A growing number of counties across the country are seeing the level of vaccination among children entering kindergarten drop below that protective threshold.

The number of children entering kindergarten whose parents or caregivers opt them out of vaccines has been steadily climbing in the U.S. for at least a decade. States differ in their requirements for vaccine exemptions, which can be for medical, religious or personal beliefs.
Jiachuan Wu is a senior graphics editor for NBC News Digital.
Jane Weaver is managing editor of the health and medical unit at NBC News.
Dr. Mustafa Fattah is a medical fellow with the NBC News Health and Medical Unit.

title_en: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder
title_zh: OpenAI 收购 Sonder 创始人创建的旅游初创公司 Odessia
summary: OpenAI has not yet said what its plans are for the future of travel. But Sonder founder Francis Davidson is a well-known figure in the travel industry.
summary_zh: OpenAI 尚未透露其对未来旅行的计划。但 Sonder 创始人弗朗西斯·戴维森 (Francis Davidson) 却是旅游业的知名人物
body_en: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder | TechCrunch

OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago. Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down.

An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the hire to TechCrunch. “We’re thrilled to welcome Francis to OpenAI. Francis is a proven founder who has built multiple businesses to help people travel, and we’re excited he’s chosen to build with us.”

However the AI lab has not announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners. Travel is also one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. And, back in July 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent , it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses.

OpenAI’s spokesperson didn’t have more to share on its plans for travel-related products, except to say that travel is one of the areas that chatbot users frequently ask about. “1.2 billion people turn to ChatGPT each week for help with everyday tasks — from understanding their health, figuring out what to make for dinner, building a budget, and even planning a trip. We see a real opportunity to make these experiences even more useful,” the spokesperson said.

Acquiring Odessia is interesting for another reason. Davidson is well known in the travel industry after he founded a travel startup called Sonder as a college student in 2014. It was sort of like Airbnb, but it focused on short-term leasing of upscale apartments in major cities worldwide. The pandemic badly hurt it, and as it climbed out of that rut, it went public via a SPAC but didn’t raise as much money as it needed, Davidson later said in a post announcing his resignation as CEO in June 2025.

When a key partnership with Marriott fell through , the company went into bankruptcy and wound down. The bankruptcy trustee sold Sonder’s name, trademarks, and website domain in 2026 to TravelAI, and that website operates as a curated guide to the kind of travel rental properties that Sonder was once known for. Prior to its downfall, Davidson had built Sonder into a unicorn with $143 million in revenues. While Sonder was not, ultimately, a success story, Davidson is the kind of battle-scarred founder that Silicon Valley often values.
So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store now with travel, now that he’s joined the company.

body_zh: OpenAI 收购 Sonder 创始人创建的旅游初创公司 Odessia | TechCrunch
Odessia 创始人 Francis Davidson 表示，OpenAI 已经收购了一家名为 Odessia 的人工智能旅行社。戴维森在宣布这笔交易的帖子中表示，他现在为 OpenAI 工作，帮助人工智能实验室打造旅行的未来。
交易条款尚未披露，但这看起来像是一次收购。戴维森的声明主要集中在他如何通过指导人工智能代理团队建立人工智能旅行社 Odessia。成立一年的 Odessia 在红杉资本领投的种子轮前筹集了 600 万美元，并在大约五个月前推出了人工智能旅行社。戴维森表示，它已经帮助早期采用者计划了价值数百万美元的旅行，但该工具已经被关闭。
OpenAI 发言人向 TechCrunch 证实了这一任命。 “我们很高兴欢迎 Francis 加入 OpenAI。Francis 是一位久经考验的创始人，他创建了多家帮助人们出行的企业，我们很高兴他选择与我们一起创建。”
不过，人工智能实验室尚未宣布新的旅行专用产品或计划。不过，它确实将 Bookings.com、Expedia 和 KAYAK 等公司视为客户或合作伙伴。旅行也是人们使用个人人工智能助理提供帮助的主要领域之一。而且，早在 2025 年 7 月，当 OpenAI 推出其 ChatGPT 代理时，它就提到旅行是其潜在用途之一。
OpenAI 的发言人没有透露更多有关旅行相关产品的计划，只是表示旅行是聊天机器人用户经常询问的领域之一。 “每周有 12 亿人向 ChatGPT 寻求日常任务方面的帮助——从了解自己的健康状况、弄清楚晚餐吃什么、制定预算，甚至计划旅行。我们看到了一个真正的机会，可以让这些体验变得更加有用，”发言人说。
收购 Odessia 之所以有趣还有另一个原因。戴维森在 2014 年还是一名大学生时创立了一家名为 Sonder 的旅游创业公司，在旅游业中广为人知。这家公司有点像 Airbnb，但专注于全球主要城市高档公寓的短期租赁。戴维森后来在 2025 年 6 月辞去首席执行官职务的帖子中表示，疫情严重伤害了该公司，当该公司摆脱困境时，该公司通过 SPAC 上市，但没有筹集到所需的资金。
当与万豪的重要合作关系破裂后，该公司破产并倒闭。破产受托人于 2026 年将 Sonder 的名称、商标和网站域名出售给 TravelAI，该网站作为 Sonder 曾经闻名的旅行租赁物业的策划指南。在倒闭之前，戴维森已将 Sonder 打造成一家营收为 1.43 亿美元的独角兽公司。虽然桑德尔最终并不是一个成功的故事，但戴维森却是硅谷经常看重的那种身经百战的创始人。
因此，既然他已经加入了 OpenAI，我们就必须拭目以待，看看 OpenAI 在旅游领域会带来什么。

title_en: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
title_zh: 随着纽约人工智能安全法生效，OpenAI、Anthropic 面临新的监管
summary: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.
summary_zh: 纽约正准备执行全面的人工智能安全法，要求 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等主要开发商注册、披露安全实践
body_en: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect | TechCrunch

New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027.

The RAISE Act , New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports.

The newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the RAISE Act and oversee large frontier AI labs. Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations.
The state also can bring enforcement actions against companies that fail to register with the new portal, though a spokesperson declined to provide specifics.

“Tech moguls tell us that their vision for AI is inevitable,” Governor Kathy Hochul said Tuesday during a press briefing. “They tell us get on board or get left behind… That any collateral damage is worth it as long as we win the race to the AI cliff.”

On Tuesday, Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research based at State University of New York’s Binghamton University. The center will independently evaluate the safety, security, and operation of advanced AI systems and work with DIGIT to review companies’ safety frameworks. Hochul first announced the center in January with $55 million in donations and capital.
“We’re building a national model for smart, sensible AI regulation, a model that puts communities above corporations and people above powerful technology,” Hochul said.

The RAISE Act isn’t the only safety law New York has passed. Last year, the state began enforcing a law that requires AI companion operators to regularly let users know they’re talking to a bot, and to make reasonable efforts to detect suicidal ideation and self-harm.

In October, Hochul signed a separate chatbot safety law for minors, restricting behaviors like deceptive human-like interactions, emotionally manipulative or sycophantic responses, and encouragement of behaviors like suicide or disordered eating. That law takes effect June 1, 2027.

Other states have also passed similar AI safety and transparency bills to the RAISE Act. California’s SB 53, which took effect in January, mandates that frontier AI labs have in place and publish safety frameworks, enact whistleblower protections, and report critical safety incidents within 15 days. Illinois’ SB 315, which will go into effect at the start of 2027, has similar requirements, plus includes independent safety compliance audits.

body_zh: 纽约人工智能安全法生效，OpenAI、Anthropic 面临新监管 | TechCrunch
纽约正在准备执行该国最重要的人工智能安全法之一。该州周二开放了一个注册门户，要求 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等大型前沿人工智能开发商在 2027 年 1 月 1 日之前注册。
纽约的安全和透明度法案《RAISE Act》将于今年年初生效。它要求大型前沿开发商（年收入超过 5 亿美元的公司）必须在其网站上发布安全框架，在 72 小时内报告重大安全事件，并发布公开模型透明度报告。
新成立的数字创新、治理、诚信和信任办公室 (DIGIT) 将实施 RAISE 法案并监督大型前沿人工智能实验室。一次违规行为的罚款最高可达 100 万美元，后续违规行为的罚款最高可达 300 万美元。
该州还可以对未能在新门户注册的公司采取执法行动，但发言人拒绝提供具体细节。
“科技巨头告诉我们，他们对人工智能的愿景是不可避免的，”州长凯西·霍赫尔 (Kathy Hochul) 在周二的新闻发布会上表示。 “他们告诉我们，要么加入，要么落后……只要我们赢得通往人工智能悬崖的竞赛，任何附带损害都是值得的。”
周二，Hochul 还在纽约州立大学宾厄姆顿大学成立了纽约人工智能责任与研究中心。该中心将独立评估先进人工智能系统的安全性、保障性和运行情况，并与 DIGIT 合作审查公司的安全框架。 Hochul 在 1 月份首次宣布该中心将获得 5500 万美元的捐款和资金。
Hochul 表示：“我们正在建立一个智能、合理的人工智能监管国家模型，该模型将社区置于企业之上，将个人置于强大的技术之上。”
《RAISE 法案》并不是纽约通过的唯一安全法。去年，该州开始执行一项法律，要求人工智能伴侣操作员定期让用户知道他们正在与机器人交谈，并做出合理的努力来检测自杀意念和自残。
10 月，Hochul 签署了一项单独的未成年人聊天机器人安全法，限制诸如欺骗性的类人互动、情感操纵或阿谀奉承的反应，以及鼓励自杀或饮食失调等行为。该法律于 2027 年 6 月 1 日生效。
其他州也通过了与 RAISE 法案类似的人工智能安全和透明度法案。加州 SB 53 于 1 月生效，要求前沿人工智能实验室建立并发布安全框架，制定举报人保护措施，并在 15 天内报告重大安全事件。伊利诺伊州的 SB 315 将于 2027 年初生效，有类似的要求，还包括独立的安全合规审计。
